title: Speak, for I hear (1 Samuel 3)
hookLine: the boy hears his name at night and answers "Speak; for Thy servant heareth"

lines: HERE AM I, YOU CALLED ME.
HE DIDN'T KNOW THE VOICE YET.
cards: It's night in the sanctuary at Shiloh. The old priest Eli is lying down in his place; his eyes have grown dim. The lamp of God hasn't gone out yet.
And the boy Samuel is asleep near the ark. Then a voice says his name. Samuel.
He runs to Eli: here am I, you called me. I didn't call, says Eli; lie down again. The voice comes again.
He runs again. And the text slips in why: Samuel did not yet know the LORD. He's hearing a voice he has no way to recognize.

teach.h: THE WORD WAS RARE IN THOSE DAYS.
teach.b: The chapter opens by setting the scene: in those days the word of the LORD was rare, and visions were not common. So when it finally comes, it comes to a boy who can't tell it from an old man's voice.
When the call comes a third time, Eli understands. And the old priest does this well. He doesn't take over.

He teaches the boy one sentence and sends him back to bed: if you are called, say, Speak, LORD; for Thy servant heareth. The LORD came and stood, the text says, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel.
And Samuel answers, "Speak; for Thy servant heareth." The answer isn't a request. Not, give me a sign.
It's, I'm here, I'm listening, go ahead.
And what he hears is hard: judgment on Eli's own house, and his sons. Samuel lies there until morning, afraid to tell the man who raised him.
Eli makes him tell everything, and hide nothing, and answers: it is the LORD; let him do what seems good to him.
So the night has two listeners: a boy learning to say speak, and an old man who hears bad news about himself and doesn't look away.

teach.h: NONE OF HIS WORDS FELL TO THE GROUND.
teach.b: The chapter ends with Samuel growing up, and the LORD letting none of his words fall to the ground.
The rare word isn't rare anymore.

how: Jews read Samuel's night call as part of the Former Prophets, and the boy's answer, speak, for thy servant heareth, is read as a picture of what it means to listen for God.

o: Eli's order to the boy to repeat the message
a command Samuel gave to the people at Shiloh
Samuel's answer: go ahead, I'm listening

games.q: the night call — tap the pairs.
p: here am I, you called me

s: Samuel recognized God's voice the first time
he ran to Eli each time. the text says he did not yet know the LORD.
Eli made Samuel tell him the whole message
he told him to hide nothing, and Samuel told him every word.
Samuel asked God for a sign
his answer asked for nothing: speak; for thy servant heareth.

games.q: you're Eli. the boy has woken you a third time, sure that you called him. what do you do?
o: tell him firmly to stop dreaming and sleep.
teach him what to answer, and send him back to listen.
go and listen for the voice yourself.
games.why: Eli understands it's God calling, and gives the boy one sentence: speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth. then he lets Samuel hear it himself.

practice: Sit or lie still, with the lights down if you can, and listen without asking for anything: the fridge, a car, your own breath, your thoughts as they come. If something keeps coming back, a name, a worry, let it come.
If you pray, say Samuel's words, speak, for thy servant heareth, and stay quiet; if you don't, simply say to yourself: I'm listening.

wordCard.voice: Speak. The word Samuel says in the dark at Shiloh, taught to him by Eli, after he'd heard his name called three times.

orig.note: Hebrew: speak, Samuel's first word back to the voice in the night.

carryVoice: Your line: here am I. The listening came before the message. Day seven hundred twenty-nine, done.
